unit.why: A medieval exemplum quoted from R. Isaac of Acre via Reshit Hokhmah (Sha'ar ha-Ahavah 4). It tells of a man whose desire for a princess turned into cleaving to God, used here to illustrate love of God.
unit.boundary_note: previous division gives the homiletic frame (love of God likened to a lover's passion); story is self-contained here

stories.start_quote: וכן נלמד ממעשה אמר שכתב הרב
stories.end_quote: עד שהלך שמו למרחוק עכ״ל לעניננו
stories.summary_en: A loafer desires a princess. Her retort 'in the cemetery' is misunderstood as a rendezvous, so he sits in the cemetery fixing his mind on her. His total concentration detaches him from all sensual things until he cleaves to God and becomes a holy man whose blessings are sought by travellers.

tags.why: Introduced with 'וכן נלמד' as an exemplum teaching love of God.
Embedded in a homiletic discussion of love of God, quoted from a musar book.

quotes: מי יתן אותה ברשותי לעשות בה כטוב בעיני
ומרוב חשקו בה הפשיט את מחשבתו מכל מורגש
tags.why: His desire for the princess drives the plot.
His soul comes to cleave to God.
Mystical cleaving is the climax of the tale.

quotes: ויום ולילה תמיד ישב בבית הקברות
tags.why: He lives secluded in the cemetery.

quotes: וקשירת מחשבת שכלו בדבר אחד תמיד
tags.why: Sustained mental concentration on a single object.

quotes: ותען בת המלך ותאמר לו בבית הקברות
tags.why: The princess's remark triggers his retreat, but she plays no further part.
Illustrates the virtue of whole-hearted love of God.

quotes: ושב להיות עובד שלם איש האלהים קדוש
tags.why: He turns from lust to holiness, though no explicit teshuvah is described.
His prayers and blessings become effective; this is ambient efficacy rather than a discrete miracle.

quotes: והיא לא נתכוונה לזה אבל רצתה לומר
tags.why: The narrator reveals the true meaning of her words, which he misunderstood.

missing_concepts: sublimation of erotic desire into love of God (ahavat ha-Shem)
misunderstood utterance as the plot device
cemetery as the setting and a symbol of equality in death
